source.display_title: 05/14/2026 - Vladtest Koc x Harry Edmonds — Follow Up

setter.evidence: No setter code in the title and no setter named anywhere on the call. The rep opened cold with no reference to prior notes.

prospect.name: Chance Lusk
prospect.occupation: Owner-operator of a construction company. Not desk-bound but not on the tools daily either — 'I'm not out there swinging a hammer every day, but there's a lot of times where I've got to go get materials for my guys and go offload them on site.'
prospect.family_status: Married to Lauren. Multiple teenage children, youngest a 13-year-old son who plays soccer. The family homeschools, so the children have no school weight room. Recently bought a family gym membership.
prospect.training_background: Former soccer player, still plays with his son. Did little training in high school and did not encounter kettlebells until around his thirties. Has a few kettlebells at home and a recently purchased gym membership, but is not training consistently — 'Not really a whole lot.' Previously dropped almost 40 lb on keto with little training and got back to 190, but says he lost muscle doing it. Prefers group classes because he does not have to think about programming. Trained with his son the morning of the call.
prospect.medical: Recurrent lower back problems over the last few years, actively managed by a chiropractor: 'usually just like lower back, stuff that can usually be treated just by going to the chiropractor and getting adjusted and taking it easy for a few days.' Acute episodes triggered by occupational lifting — carrying 60 lb bags of concrete mix on site, then 'the next day, I'll go pick up a hanger, and it's like, oh, there goes my back.' His stated posture toward it has been avoidance rather than rehabilitation: 'a lot of that's just like, don't do anything to mess it up, but it's not really, hey, go back in and make it stronger.' High occupational stress and self-identified stress eater. No imaging, diagnosis or physician involvement mentioned.

signals: Actively losing ground and aware of it: 'I notice it a lot of just like not being as strong as I used to be, go play a long ball and it's like, oh, that was 20 yards short of where I thought I could get it to'

Wants a former self back with a specific number attached: 225 lb now, 'would definitely like to be more like in that one 90 or lower. I don't think I've been less than 190 in at least a decade or more'
Regret framed around appearance rather than performance: 'I would love to not hate the way I look whenever I take my shirt off'
A hard season is the cause — a construction business, high stress, stress eating and no mental capacity left for programming
Not the optimizer: he is not moving from good to great, he is trying to arrest a decline. 'I feel like I'm losing that day by day.'
Not the preserver either — he has plenty of liquidity and wants to gain ground, not just hold it

goals.text: Get back to a level of fitness where he can do what he wants with his teenagers
Be functionally fit — his own words for his biggest goal
Build a training habit his 13-year-old son will copy, and have something they do together, since homeschooling means no school weight room
Get from 225 lb to 190 or below, while getting stronger rather than losing muscle as he did on keto
Make his back stronger rather than merely avoiding aggravating it
Protect and rebuild leg and trunk strength so he can still play soccer and hit a long ball
Find something consistent enough to survive travel and stressful seasons — 'no excuse for not carrying on'
Stop having to think about programming — he has no mental capacity left for it
Avoid spending money on healthcare later by taking care of himself now
Not hate the way he looks with his shirt off, without trying to be a fitness model

pains.text: Recurrent lower back episodes requiring chiropractic adjustment and days of rest, triggered by occupational lifting
Consistency collapses when routine breaks — travel, vacations and stressful seasons, and once a day is missed the next is easier to miss
No mental capacity to build a training plan on top of running a business — 'building out a training program is just not my skillset'
Stress eating driven by the business
Losing strength measurably, especially legs, and can feel it on the pitch
Has never been good with nutrition and does not want another diet
Previous success came at a cost — lost 40 lb on keto but believes he lost muscle with it
Dislikes his own appearance with his shirt off
Worried his homeschooled son will fall behind physically without a structured route to training

objections.raw_quote: I mean, I'm definitely interested. I mean, that money is always a question. So that's always a huge piece, but you know, what's the, uh, also understand that things cost money too.
objections.rep_response: Pre-empted with a single line before the number was even quoted: 'It'll be cheaper than surgery in 10 years if you needed it.' No isolation, no financial exploration.

objections.raw_quote: what would be next steps if I, cause I'm, I mean, I don't usually do anything without at least talking about it with my wife, praying about it some, um, it's not a small chunk of change. So I would like to at least make sure that I'm not doing something fiscally irresponsible at this point as well.
objections.rep_response: Ran the play properly and nearly in full. Asked her name, asked whether she is supportive of the journey, asked what she has already been told, ran the two-reactions framing and got an honest prediction, produced the guarantee specifically as ammunition for that conversation, isolated personal commitment twice ('is it something that you want to do most importantly?' and 'Are you sure? I just want to make sure'), then closed the scripted fallback: a $100 refundable deposit plus a booked follow-up call for 4pm the next day. The prospect paid it live on the call.

offer.payment_plan_terms: No instalment plan offered. A separate $100 refundable holding deposit was taken live via a Stripe link in the Zoom chat, framed as standard practice on follow-ups: 'What we usually do is just take a small deposit. It's a hundred bucks. It's refundable... if she says I'm literally going to throw you in the river, then we just shoot you the hundred bucks back.'
offer.guarantee_mentioned: 'We have a guarantee, so everything's guaranteed... The guarantee is that over six months, you will put on eight kilos on a kettlebell. So from the starting kettlebell weight to the end, you put on eight kilos on every lift... if you do everything we say, and that isn't met, then we work with you for free until you're at that level anyway. So the results are guaranteed.' Introduced explicitly as leverage for the spouse conversation: 'I don't know even why it slipped my mind, just so you can mention it to her as well.'

prospect_financials.note: No financial-picture questions were asked. Affordability was inferred from behaviour and self-assessment: he owns the business, paid the $100 deposit within seconds, and framed the price as immaterial over a long horizon — 'six grand seems like a drop in the bucket over the long haul'. The rep raised putting it through the business as a write-off.

evidence: A $100 refundable holding deposit was paid live on the call via Stripe — 'Yeah, I just paid it just now' / 'Yeah, I just got it' — but this is a hold, not payment for the programme
The purchase decision is expressly not made: 'I don't usually do anything without at least talking about it with my wife, praying about it some'
The deposit was framed as fully reversible by that conversation: 'if she says I'm literally going to throw you in the river, then we just shoot you the hundred bucks back'

Strong counter-evidence toward a close: firm personal commitment when isolated — 'I think I would be on board to make it happen' and 'six grand seems like a drop in the bucket over the long haul' — plus a stated preference to move fast, 'I would like to get something going pretty quickly if it's a yes'
A specific follow-up call was booked for 4pm Central the next day, ahead of a 5:15 commitment, and the rep described the onboarding as 15 minutes including processing payment
Six-month tier selected: 'I mean, probably 6 months'

Note on classification: a literal reading of the close rule could be argued here, since the prospect verbally leaned in and a payment link was sent and paid. It is recorded as follow_up because the link was for a $100 refundable hold rather than the $6,000 programme, and because the prospect explicitly reserved the decision for his wife. Flagging this so the rollup can see the boundary case rather than inheriting a silent judgement.
outcome.next_step: Prospect to speak to his wife Lauren and pray on it overnight; booked follow-up call with the rep at 4pm Central the following day, at which payment would be processed and onboarding completed if it is a yes. Trevor onboarding call indicated for Monday or Tuesday but not booked.

notable.note: Two things stand out. First, the file title names a completely different person — 'Vladtest Koc' — while the prospect on the recording is Chance Lusk, an Amarillo construction company owner; any join on title will be wrong. Second, the rep offered to help structure a personal fitness purchase as a business tax write-off: '70% roughly of our clients are business owners. So we're very, very used to framing it in a way that you can write it off as well. So if you need help with that, we'll help you write it off. It's always good when it's almost free.' That is unqualified tax advice from a sales rep. On the positive side this is the best-run objection sequence in the batch — the spouse play was executed close to in full and terminated correctly in the scripted refundable deposit, the only call in the batch where that happened. The prospect also has recurrent lower back problems under active chiropractic care and was guaranteed an eight-kilogram load increase on every kettlebell movement, with no clinician clearance sought.

quality.notes: Severe and structural — the labels are inverted for most of the call. The rep's frame at 00:01:01 is labelled 'Chance Lusk'; the entire offer walkthrough from 00:16:05 to 00:22:23 is labelled 'Harry Edmonds' but contains the prospect's replies inside it; the price quote at 00:23:13 is labelled Harry while 'You own the business?' at 00:23:34 is labelled Chance and is plainly the rep. The block at 00:11:00-00:12:00 attributes the rep's entire missed-a-day observation to the prospect. Roles resolved from content throughout. The Fathom transcriber also renders 'fat' as 'Fath' in places.
